- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 5 days.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–2% per day until price stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is >10% above true outcome, reduce by 1–2% per day for next 5 days; if below, add 0.5–1% per day.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model often misjudges momentum; adjust forecast to align with sentiment trend direction, not peak.
